reading: Two coloured cells sit on opposite long edges; each draws a full line across the short dimension, and the pair of lines repeats with the same spacing, alternating colours, to the far end of the grid.

slots.direction: lines run across the short side of the grid, perpendicular to the long axis
slots.period: distance between the two markers along the long axis; colours alternate A, B, A, B ... from the first marker to the end

why: each marker's line spans the full short dimension, and lines recur every 2*d along the long axis starting from each marker
invariants: cells before the first marker stay background

reading: Each isolated cell gets a colour-specific pattern around it: red (2) gets yellow (4) at its four diagonals, blue (1) gets orange (7) at its four orthogonal neighbours, other colours (8, 6) get nothing.
why: around every marker of colour c the same pattern for c is drawn, centred on the marker
every cell of colour a becomes key(a), same key on all pairs

reading: Blue (1) cells on opposite borders are joined by a full blue line; every red (2) rectangle the line crosses turns entirely blue.

new_rows.name: crossed
new_rows.datalog:
hitobj(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C), C = 2, off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, D), D = 1.
crossed(Y, X) :- hitobj(O), obj(O, Y, X).

why: the line runs border to border through the marker pair; every 2-object touching the line becomes 1 and other 2-objects are unchanged
invariants: red rectangles not crossed by a line

reading: Each isolated cell draws a full horizontal line on its row; the grid is split into horizontal bands at the midpoints between markers, and each band's left and right edge columns (plus the grid's top row for the first band and bottom row for the last) take that marker's colour.

slots.sources: the isolated cells (markers), sorted by row
slots.bands: rows from midpoint to midpoint between consecutive markers; first band starts at row 0, last ends at the bottom row
slots.drawn: full row at each marker, left and right border cells of its band, top border row in the first band, bottom border row in the last band

why: every border cell and every marker row is coloured by the marker owning that band
invariants: interior cells off the marker rows stay background

reading: A small multi-coloured template and a large grey (8) shape that is the template rotated 90 degrees clockwise and scaled up; each block of the large shape is recoloured with the colour of the matching template cell.

slots.transform: template rotated 90 degrees clockwise, scaled by target size / template size (3 in pair 1, 2 in pair 2)
slots.action: each k x k block of the target takes the colour of the corresponding rotated template cell

why: the target's block mask equals the non-background mask of the rotated template

reading: The input is tiled 2x2, then every coloured cell gets azure (8) on each diagonal neighbour that is background.
why: output is the 2x2 tiling with 8 written on background diagonal neighbours of each non-background cell, clipped at the grid edge
invariants: the tiled coloured cells keep their colour

reading: Three cells mark the corners of a right triangle; at the midpoint of the hypotenuse a grey (5) cell is placed, and each corner's colour is copied to the diagonal neighbour of that midpoint pointing toward that corner.

slots.centre: midpoint of the two corners that differ in both row and column
slots.copies: each corner colour at centre + (sign(dy), sign(dx)) toward that corner

why: exactly four new cells appear, all within one step of the hypotenuse midpoint

reading: Every single-colour 4-connected piece of fewer than 3 cells becomes green (3); larger pieces keep their colour.

new_rows.name: small4
new_rows.datalog:
adj(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, Y2 = Y, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
adj(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X, cell(Y2, X2, C).
reach(Y, X, Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
reach(Y, X, Y3, X3) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2), adj(Y2, X2, Y3, X3).
size(Y, X, count(Y2, X2)) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2).
small4(Y, X) :- size(Y, X, N), N < 3.

why: a cell changes to 3 exactly when its 4-connected same-colour component has size 1 or 2

reading: A full-length grey (5) wall lies on one border; every coloured segment parallel to it sweeps toward the wall, filling the band between itself and the wall, and stops at the first coloured cell (another segment or the wall).
why: each segment cell extends perpendicular to its segment toward the wall and stops just before the first non-background cell, so a nearer segment is never overpainted
invariants: cells on the far side of each segment from the wall
